downgraded.text: Met in the bath (banya) at late hours, when people bathe at night.
downgraded.reason: Ralston p.123 says the domovoy is known as the Bannik "when he haunts a bath (banya)" and that peasants avoid the bath at late hours; it does not say he is met or encountered there at late hours. The encounter-at-late-hours framing is inference and was cut.

flagged.reason: afanasyev1868 p.69 prints "баннаго" only as the genitive in "названія баннаго (банника)"; the form is printed as the native row requires, but a genitive inflection is recorded as a name variant. Its nominative (банный) is not printed on the page, so it cannot be substituted without adding content.

grade_rationale.text: The only people named in the verified entry is the Russians (one general row and one Smolensk Government row).
Afanasyev names the bannik as the domovoy living in the bath-house and gives its haunts, sounds, night-time suffocation and the Smolensk shelf saying and bucket-and-whisk custom.
Ralston names the Bannik as the domovoy haunting the bath and gives the night-bathing danger and the Smolensk bucket-and-whisk custom; his bannik passage cites and quotes no source.

Ralston cites Afanasyev two pages earlier for a different domovoy custom (footnote 8, "Afanasief, P. V. S. ii. 67"), not for the bannik passage, so under the per-passage rule the two are counted as two independent sources; his p.123 passage nevertheless follows the order and details of Afanasyev p.69 closely.
One people with two independent authors grades regional.
